label: What a denoiser predicts at each noise level
context: Same two-moons data (≈300 faint grey points). One highlighted noisy query point x moves along a path. For the query, show the denoiser's optimal output D(x, σ) = E[x_0 | x_σ = x], computed exactly as the softmax-weighted mean of all data points with weights exp(-|x - x_i|² / (2σ²)); draw it as a filled blue dot with an arrow from x to D(x, σ). Also draw a few data points with line opacity proportional to their weight. Cycle sigma through three levels and hold each about 4 s: high σ (D sits near the mean of the whole dataset, between the moons; caption 'high σ: the best guess is the average of everything'), medium σ (D jumps to the nearest crescent; caption 'medium σ: which crescent?'), low σ (D lands on the nearest data point; caption 'low σ: just clean up the detail'). Show a σ gauge. The point: the same network solves very different problems at different σ. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: What the optimal denoiser predicts at each noise level
spec.caption: For a noisy query x, the optimal denoiser D(x, σ) is the softmax-weighted mean of all data points, with weights exp(-|x - xᵢ|²/(2σ²)). At high σ it returns the average of everything. At medium σ it commits to one crescent. At low σ it snaps to the nearest data point. The same network has to solve all three problems.
